title: ATOMS: ALMA three-millimeter observations of massive star-forming regions - XVIII. On the origin and evolution of dense gas fragments in molecular shells of compact H II regions
question: How do compact H II regions affect the properties and origin of dense gas fragments embedded in their molecular shells (CCH shells, H13CO+ fragments)?

recipe.goal: Reduce and image the ATOMS Band 3 data
recipe.method: CASA 5.6 tclean on combined main array and 7 m array data with natural weighting
key_parameters: Imaged field to 20% power point, radius 44 arcsec

recipe.goal: Select compact H II regions with CCH molecular shells
recipe.method: Examine CCH and H40alpha distributions in all 146 ATOMS fields and select by two criteria (prominent CCH shell at the edge of H40alpha emission; H40alpha well resolved)
assumptions: CCH is a sensitive tracer of the photodissociation region

recipe.goal: Derive H II region size, ionization rate, spectral type, electron density, pressure
recipe.method: Size from H40alpha moment 0 mask edges; ionization rate from H40alpha luminosity assuming ionization-recombination equilibrium; ne from the effective volume; Pi from ne and ionized-gas sound speed
key_parameters: epsilon = 1.99e-32, b_ul = 0.788, f_ul(LTE) = 7.03e-19 cm3, A_ul = 54.7 s-1, alpha_B = 2.54e-13 cm3 s-1
assumptions: Te = 1e4 K and ne = 1e4 cm-3 for the efficiency factor; helium ionization ignored
Te from the Galactocentric distance relation when not measured

recipe.goal: Estimate initial density and dynamical age of the H II regions
recipe.method: n_ini from ATLASGAL clump properties in two cases (SExtractor mass/radius; peak column density/GaussClump FWHM); t_dyn from Dyson1997 with Stromgren radius
assumptions: Average clump density does not change much from quiescent to H II region stage (difference ~20%)

recipe.goal: Extract dense gas fragments from the H13CO+ cubes
recipe.method: 3D astrodendro dendrogram on cubes without PB correction; leaves are fragments
key_parameters: min_npix equivalent to three channels x half of the beam size
pruning: min_peak = 4.5 rms, minimum three channels, minimum spatial size half a beam

recipe.goal: Measure fragment properties (sigma, mass, surface density, density, virial ratio)
recipe.method: Gaussian fit to the average spectrum within the dendrogram area and velocity range; optically thin H13CO+ column density with Tex = Tdust; mass from column density and abundance; Sigma, n_H2 and virial ratio from the dendrogram effective radius
key_parameters: Virial ratio R_vir = 5 sigma^2 r / (M G)
assumptions: Tex equals the clump-scale dust temperature
Constant density profile, no magnetic field, rotation or external pressure for the virial ratio

recipe.goal: Classify fragments as N (near H II region) or F (far) and compare their properties
recipe.method: Extend each fragment by a beam width and measure overlap with the H II region; N if overlap > 50% of the extended fragment or mean H40alpha in the overlap > 10% of the peak; compare sigma, sigma_NT, mass, Sigma, n_H2, R_vir with K-S tests; regression of sigma_NT against radius
key_parameters: sigma_NT from sigma and Tkin (N: Tdust+5 K, F: Tdust-5 K); Tex varied the same way for mass tests
assumptions: N fragments are warmer than F fragments by about 10 K in total

recipe.goal: Test spatial regulation of fragments by the H II region
recipe.method: Angular two-point correlation function (Landy-Szalay) between H II region position and fragments, normalized by its peak and r_eff; photoevaporation mass loss rate estimated with the Haworth2012 equation
key_parameters: Typical fragment radius 0.04 pc; ionizing photon rate 1e48 s-1; distances 0.1 to 0.2 pc
assumptions: Initial fragments randomly distributed in space (first explanation)

recipe.goal: Measure fragment kinematics relative to the H II region
recipe.method: PV cuts of H13CO+ and CCH, and histograms of v_frag - v_HII with Gaussian fits; v_HII from Gaussian fit to the averaged H40alpha spectrum of the whole emission region
key_parameters: Histogram dispersion difference N vs F about 1.7 km/s; measure error 0.1-0.2 km/s

recipe.goal: Test shell fragmentation (collect and collapse) and Jeans fragmentation origins
recipe.method: Compute t_frag, r_frag, M_frag, D_frag from the Whitworth1994 equations with two n_ini cases and clump-scale sound speed; compare with H II region age and size and with observed fragment mass and MST separations; compare MST separations with Jeans length
key_parameters: Sound speed from the ATLASGAL dust temperature (clump-scale)
assumptions: Expansion law R ~ K t^(4/7) of the classical model

recipe.goal: Assess the role of stellar winds
recipe.method: C_w factor of Geen2020 for two natal cloud cases; wind-driven shell fragmentation times of Whitworth1994
key_parameters: Clump case r0 = 0.5 pc, n0 = 1e4 cm-3; Nion = 1e48 s-1

recipe.goal: Examine fragment mass growth and fragment-to-clump mass ratio
recipe.method: Compare fragment mass with H II region size; ratio of total N fragment mass to ATLASGAL clump mass
assumptions: Fragment (H13CO+) and clump (dust) masses use different mass probes, so the absolute ratio may be biased
